localChanges: A turn-1 save was 1.6MB of JSON, and JSON of the most compressible kind: every entity repeats the same field names and most of the file is references like `{"$ref":"Tile-1f4"}`. Gzipped through `CompressionStream` it loses 93% — measured on a real save, 838KB to 55KB — and loading detects the gzip header, so files written either way still open. Without `CompressionStream` the save is written as plain JSON: a save that cannot be written would be worse than a large one.

The name came out as `The English 16x2F09x2F2026.civ-clone.json`. i18next escapes interpolated values for HTML, so the localised date arrived as `16/09/2026`, and stripping the punctuation left `x2F` behind. The default name is built from plain parts now — civilisation, turn and an ISO date — and the sanitiser only removes what a file name cannot hold: `The English, turn 1, 2026-09-16.civ-clone.json.gz`.
